section_heading: Understand the causes of layout shifts

supports.section: Understand the causes of layout shifts
supports.excerpt:
In some cases adding content dynamically is an important part of user experience. For example, when loading more products to a list of items or when updating live feed content. There are several ways to avoid unexpected layout shifts in those cases:

- Replace the old content with the new content within a fixed size container or use a carousel and remove the old content after the transition. Remember to disable any links and controls until the transition has completed to prevent accidental clicks or taps while the new content is coming in.

- Have the user initiate the load of new content, so they are not surprised by the shift (for example with a "Load more" or "Refresh" button). It's recommended to prefetch the content before the user interaction so that it shows up immediately. As a reminder, layout shifts that occur within 500 milliseconds of user input are not counted towards CLS.

- Seamlessly load the content offscreen and overlay a notice to the user that it's available (for example, with a "Scroll to top" button).

Examples of dynamic content loading without causing unexpected layout shifts. Left: Live feed content loading on Twitter. Right: "Load More" example on Chloé website. Check out how the YNAP team optimized for CLS when loading more content.

skill_drafts.name: Dynamic Content Loading with Layout Stability
skill_drafts.description: Workflow for loading new content dynamically (e.g., product lists, live feeds) while preventing unexpected layout shifts. Provides three patterns: fixed-size containers with carousels, user-initiated loading triggers, and offscreen preloading with user notification.
skill_drafts.objective: Prevent cumulative layout shift (CLS) during dynamic content insertion while maintaining responsive user experience
applicable_signals: Product list pagination or 'Load more' interaction
Dynamic content insertion into existing page layout
User expects seamless content refresh without visual disruption
contraindications: Content is static or pre-rendered at page load
User interaction is not feasible or desired
Layout shifts are intentional or user-initiated and expected
intervention_moves: Use fixed-size container or carousel to constrain new content dimensions
Disable links and controls during content transition to prevent accidental interaction
Trigger content load via explicit user action (button click) rather than automatic insertion
Prefetch content before user interaction to ensure immediate display
Load new content offscreen and notify user of availability via overlay notice
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify dynamic content insertion point and choose pattern', 'detail': 'Determine whether fixed-container, user-initiated, or offscreen-load pattern best fits use case'}

{'step': 2, 'action': 'Implement chosen pattern', 'detail': "Pattern A (fixed container): Define container dimensions, replace old content with new within container, disable controls during transition. Pattern B (user-initiated): Add 'Load more' or 'Refresh' button, prefetch content on page load or after previous interaction, trigger display on button click. Pattern C (offscreen): Load content offscreen, overlay user-facing notice (e.g., 'Scroll to top' button) to signal availability"}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Verify CLS impact', 'detail': 'Measure CLS score before and after implementation; confirm no unexpected layout shifts occur during content insertion'}

{'step': 4, 'action': 'Test user interaction responsiveness', 'detail': 'Ensure controls remain responsive and transitions complete without lag; verify no accidental clicks or taps occur during transition'}
triggers: Implementing product list pagination, live feed updates, or any dynamic content insertion that could cause visual instability
constraints: Layout shifts occurring within 500 milliseconds of user input are not counted toward CLS; ensure user interaction precedes content insertion by at least this margin
Fixed-size containers must have dimensions known before content load
Carousel transitions must complete before re-enabling user controls
Offscreen preloading requires sufficient memory and bandwidth
cautions: Disabling controls during transition may feel unresponsive if transition is too long; keep duration brief
Prefetching increases bandwidth usage; monitor for performance impact on slower connections
Offscreen loading with overlay notice may be missed by users if notice is not prominent
output_contract: New content loads without unexpected layout shifts; CLS score remains unaffected or improves; user interactions remain responsive during transition; content appears immediately (for user-initiated and prefetch patterns) or is clearly signaled as available (for offscreen pattern)

examples.input: Live feed application needs to insert new posts without shifting existing content
examples.output: Load new posts offscreen, overlay 'New posts available' notice; user clicks notice to scroll to top and view new content. CLS remains stable.
examples.notes: Offscreen pattern; user controls when to view new content

examples.output: User clicks 'Load more' button; content is prefetched and inserted into fixed-height container below current list. Controls disabled during 200ms transition. CLS unaffected.
examples.notes: User-initiated pattern with prefetch; transition time kept brief

examples.input: Image carousel with dynamic content replacement
examples.output: Old carousel item replaced with new item within fixed-size container; navigation controls disabled until transition completes. CLS stable.
examples.notes: Fixed-container pattern; carousel ensures predictable dimensions

metadata.prompt: When implementing dynamic content insertion, choose one of three approaches: (1) Replace old content with new content within a fixed-size container or carousel, disabling controls until transition completes; (2) Have the user initiate the load via a button (e.g., 'Load more', 'Refresh'), prefetching content beforehand so it appears immediately; or (3) Load content offscreen and overlay a notice (e.g., 'Scroll to top' button) to inform the user. All three patterns avoid unexpected layout shifts and preserve CLS performance.

skill_drafts.name: User-Initiated Content Load Pattern
skill_drafts.description: Micro-interaction where user explicitly triggers new content load via button (e.g., 'Load More' or 'Refresh') with prefetched content to ensure immediate display and avoid surprise layout shifts.
skill_drafts.objective: Enable user control over content loading to prevent unexpected layout shifts and improve perceived performance.
applicable_signals: User expects to control when new content appears
Prefetching is feasible within the application architecture
Layout shift elimination is a performance requirement
Content can be loaded in advance without user awareness
contraindications: Real-time automatic updates are required by the application
User interaction cannot be added to the content load flow
Content must load without user awareness or initiation
Prefetching is not technically feasible or would consume excessive resources
intervention_moves: Add a 'Load More' or 'Refresh' button that user can click to trigger content load
Prefetch content in the background before user interaction
Ensure content appears immediately upon user click
Verify no layout shifts occur after content insertion
workflow_steps: Identify content that will be loaded dynamically
Implement prefetch mechanism to load content before user interaction
Create user-facing button or control (e.g., 'Load More', 'Refresh')
Bind button click to display prefetched content
Measure layout shift timing relative to user input
Confirm shifts occur within 500ms window (not counted toward CLS)
triggers: User expects to control when new content appears; prefetching is feasible; layout shifts must be eliminated
constraints: Content must be prefetched before user interaction to ensure immediate display
User interaction must be explicit and intentional
Layout shifts must be measured and verified to occur within 500ms of input
cautions: Prefetching may increase initial bandwidth usage; monitor resource consumption
Ensure button is accessible and clearly communicates its purpose
Test across network conditions to verify prefetched content loads in time
output_contract: User clicks button; prefetched content appears immediately without layout shift; any shifts that occur are within 500 milliseconds of user input and do not count toward Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) metric.

metadata.prompt: When implementing user-initiated content loading: (1) Prefetch content before the user interaction so it displays immediately upon click. (2) Ensure the user explicitly triggers the load via a clear button or control. (3) Verify that layout shifts occur within 500 milliseconds of user input, which are not counted toward CLS. (4) Test that no unexpected shifts occur after content appears.

skill_drafts.name: Fixed-Size Container for Content Replacement
skill_drafts.description: Micro-technique using a fixed-dimension container or carousel to swap old content with new content, with disabled controls during transition to prevent accidental interaction and maintain layout stability.
skill_drafts.objective: Maintain layout stability when replacing content by constraining container dimensions and preventing user interaction during transition
applicable_signals: New content is ready to display
Old content needs to be replaced
contraindications: Content size varies unpredictably or cannot be constrained
Container dimensions cannot be fixed without breaking design
Layout must adapt to variable content heights or widths
workflow_steps: Set fixed dimensions on the container element before content swap
Disable all interactive elements (links, buttons, form controls) within the container
Initiate transition animation to swap old content with new content
Wait for transition animation to complete (typically 300–500 milliseconds)
Remove old content from DOM
Re-enable interactive elements
Verify no layout shift occurred
triggers: Dynamic content replacement is required (e.g., loading more products, updating feed items)
Carousel or fixed-box UI pattern is appropriate for the use case
constraints: Container dimensions must be set before content swap begins
All interactive controls must remain disabled during transition
Transition duration should be brief to minimize user wait time
Old content must be removed only after transition completes
cautions: If controls are not disabled, users may accidentally click or tap during transition
If container size is not fixed, layout shift will occur and CLS will increase
Ensure transition timing is consistent across browsers and devices
output_contract: Old content successfully replaced with new content within the same container bounds; no layout shift occurs; Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) metric remains unaffected; all controls remain disabled until transition completes; container footprint is unchanged before, during, and after swap.

metadata.prompt: When replacing content dynamically, use a fixed-size container or carousel to hold both old and new content. Ensure the container dimensions are predetermined and do not change during the swap. Disable all interactive elements (links, buttons, controls) within the container until the transition animation completes. Remove the old content after the transition finishes. This approach prevents unexpected layout shifts by keeping the container footprint constant.

skill_drafts.name: Offscreen Preload with User Notification
skill_drafts.description: Load new content outside the viewport while displaying a non-intrusive notification (e.g., 'Scroll to top' button) to inform the user of available content without causing layout shift.
skill_drafts.objective: Load content without visual disruption and notify user of availability
applicable_signals: Live feed updates or product list expansions
Content availability without immediate visibility requirement
User preference for control over content discovery
contraindications: Immediate content visibility is required for user task completion
Offscreen rendering is not supported by the platform or browser
Notification overlay conflicts with existing UI patterns
Content must be visible in the initial viewport
workflow_steps: Preload new content in an offscreen container or hidden DOM element
Render the content without triggering layout recalculation in the visible viewport
Display a non-intrusive notification (e.g., 'Scroll to top' button) to alert the user
Ensure the notification is accessible and clearly indicates new content is available
Allow user to navigate to the new content on demand
Verify that no layout shift occurs during preload or notification display
triggers: Dynamic content needs to be added to the page
Content can be rendered outside the current viewport
User should be informed of new content availability
Seamless, non-disruptive experience is a priority
constraints: Preload content before displaying the notification to ensure immediate availability when user navigates
Keep notification non-intrusive and visually minimal
Ensure notification is accessible and clearly communicates that new content is available
cautions: Test offscreen rendering performance to avoid memory or rendering issues
Verify notification placement does not obscure critical UI elements
Confirm user can easily navigate to the new content from the notification
output_contract: Content loads offscreen without causing layout shift (CLS remains zero or minimal); notification appears and is visible to user; user can navigate to new content; no unexpected visual disruption occurs.

metadata.prompt: When adding content dynamically and seamless user experience is the priority: preload the content offscreen, then overlay a notice to the user that new content is available. This prevents unexpected layout shifts while keeping the user informed. Ensure the notification is non-intrusive and allows the user to navigate to the new content when ready.
